cards.text: It's the day after Jesus fed that huge crowd. The people still on that side of the sea notice something strange: only one boat was there, the disciples left in it alone, and Jesus never got on. Then some boats from Tiberias land nearby.

cards.question: The crowd sees that Jesus and His disciples are both gone. Where do they take the boats to look for Him?

cards.text: They find Jesus on the other side of the sea and ask, "Rabbi, when did You get here?" That's the look you give a coworker who beat you to the office when you KNOW you had the only car.

cards.question: Jesus skips the when and goes straight to the why. Why does He say the crowd is looking for Him?

answers.text: They ate the loaves and had their fill
They saw Him walking on the sea
They want Him to heal their sick

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them, "Do not work for food that perishes." Friend, I know ALL about food that perishes. My best batch of the week? Stale by Thursday.

cards.question: Instead, Jesus says to work for food that endures to ___ life, which the Son of Man will give.

cards.text: Jesus adds that God the Father has placed His seal of approval on the Son of Man. So the crowd asks, "What must we do to perform the works of God?"

cards.question: Jesus answers that the work of God is to ___ in the One He has sent.

cards.text: Now they ask Jesus what sign He'll perform so they can see it and believe Him. Friend, these folks ate miracle bread YESTERDAY, and today it's "Okay... but what ELSE You got?"

cards.question: To make their point, the crowd brings up what their fathers ate in the wilderness. What was it?

cards.text: They even quote Scripture about it: "He gave them bread from heaven to eat." Jesus answers them with a "Truly, truly."

cards.question: Jesus agrees with the crowd that Moses gave them the bread from heaven.

cards.text: Jesus says His Father gives the true bread from heaven, and the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world. The crowd is IN: "Sir, give us this bread at all times."
Jesus answers, "I am the bread of life." He doesn't just HAND them the bread, friend. He IS the bread.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever comes to Him will never ___, and whoever believes in Him will never ___.

cards.text: But Jesus tells them, "you have seen Me and still you do not believe." Then He makes a promise about everyone the Father gives Him.

cards.question: Jesus promises He will never drive away the one who comes to Him.

cards.text: Jesus says He came down from heaven, not to do His own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Him.

cards.question: What does Jesus say is the will of the One who sent Him, for those the Father has given Him?

answers.text: That He lose none of them
That He judge each of them
That He send them all out

cards.question: Jesus says it's His Father's will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life.

cards.text: We're still with the crowd in Capernaum, where Jesus has said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven." Now the Jews there start to grumble about Him. It's like hearing the guy from down the street announce he's royalty.

cards.question: The grumblers can't see how Jesus came down from heaven. What do they point to?

answers.text: They know His father and mother

cards.text: They ask, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" Jesus replies, "Stop grumbling among yourselves."

cards.question: Jesus says no one can come to Him unless the Father who sent Him draws him.

cards.text: Jesus quotes the Prophets: "And they will all be taught by God." Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Jesus.

cards.question: Jesus says no one has seen the Father except the One who is from God.

cards.text: Then another "Truly, truly." Whoever believes has eternal life, and Jesus says that line again: "I am the bread of life."

cards.question: Jesus says their fathers who ate the manna in the wilderness never died.

cards.text: Jesus says this bread comes down from heaven so anyone may eat of it and not die. "I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever."

cards.question: Jesus says the bread He will give for the life of the world is His ___.

cards.text: The Jews start arguing among themselves: "How can this man give us His flesh to eat?" Friend, I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries that argued for YEARS about who had the most charge left, so I know what a big argument sounds like.

cards.question: Jesus doesn't back down. What does He say about anyone who doesn't eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man?

answers.text: They have no life in them

cards.text: Whoever eats His flesh and drinks His blood has eternal life, and Jesus will raise him up at the last day. "For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink."

cards.question: What else does Jesus say about whoever eats His flesh and drinks His blood?

answers.text: He remains in Jesus and Jesus in him
He sees the Father face to face
He rules the land with Jesus

cards.text: Then Jesus makes a comparison. Just as the living Father sent Him and He lives because of the Father, the one who feeds on Him will live because of Him.

cards.question: Jesus sums it up by comparing two kinds of bread. Unlike the fathers who ate the manna and died, what about the one who eats this bread?
Jesus said all this while teaching in the ___ in Capernaum.

cards.text: I bet that room had a LOT to chew on. Hang on, friend. This story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "Do not work for food that perishes.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "but what ELSE You got?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "Sir, give us this bread at all times.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 3 quotes "Stop grumbling among yourselves.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the moment. In the coworker joke, you had the only car. But the crowd never had the boat. The disciples left in it (John 6:22). The comparison's action, being beaten somewhere by someone with no ride while you held the only ride, doesn't line up with the crowd's situation, so it reads as 'huh?'.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'Quail' is a wrong answer, but Israel's fathers also ate quail in the wilderness (Exodus 16:13; Numbers 11:31-32). A baker could argue it's right for 'what their fathers ate in the wilderness.'

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card tells that Jesus answers with 'Truly, truly,' which is John 6:32, but it cites only John 6:31. It should cite John 6:31-32.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The statement says the crowd claimed Moses gave them the bread from heaven. In John 6:31 the crowd only quotes 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat' and never names Moses. The card fills in who 'He' is, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats: the Father gives the true bread (6:32), the bread of God is He who comes down and gives life (6:33), and the crowd asks for this bread (6:34).

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The joke 'the guy from down the street' tells the baker the grumblers know Jesus personally. That gives away the answer to card 2 ('They know His father and mother') and rules out the wrong answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The battery joke ends by explaining itself: 'so I know what a big argument sounds like.'
Card 9 already told the baker 'he will live forever' (John 6:51). Card 16 then asks about the same line repeated in John 6:58, so the earlier card gives the answer away.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: Many story cards are bare paraphrase with no Papa Dorin voice or humor: stop 1 cards 7, 13, 16 and 18, and stop 2 cards 3, 5, 9, 13 and 15. Those stretches read like a plain summary, not Papa Dorin telling the story.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
